order: This change makes the guard hook read the session's own model first, and it decides whether to deny a tool call. Enforcement now applies to director models alone while every other model stands the guard down entirely, with no partial state in between the two. An undetermined model still resolves to enforce rather than stand down, and the harness can never silently vanish for an actual director session under ambiguous conditions. The latest non-sidechain assistant model alone gets read from the transcript, using a fixed-cost tail read, and sidechain entries are skipped so a finished scout run under a different model is never mistaken for the session's own. Reading the latest turn alone means a mid-session model switch gets honored right away rather than through a stale cached value, and detection runs solely on the would-deny path, so an allowed call pays nothing extra. The docs then get updated to describe the new behavior in full.
claims: Detection runs only on the would-deny path, so allowed calls pay nothing extra, and the measured cost came out at roughly zero added time over the existing spawn cost on an 8.8MB transcript. The guard now enforces solely for director models and stands down entirely for any other model, while an undetermined model still resolves to enforce rather than stand down from it. The change touches three files in all, and the docs were revised to describe the new behavior throughout.
